clue.text: America releasing first person shot with this?

definitions.text: America releasing first person shot with this?

indicators.note: releasing says a letter is let go from the word America before the rest is worked
shot in the sense of broken up or ruined, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A tourist wonders what device took a photo of someone in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of AMERICA and rearrange the remaining AMERCA ('shot'); the whole clue also describes the answer, since a person can be shot with one.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer shoots a subject with a lens-and-shutter device, the pun on shooting someone.

clue.text: Pressure in dysfunctional families builds up

indicators.note: in puts one letter inside the rearranged word
dysfunctional means not working properly, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Stress within troubled households keeps on mounting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dysfunctional' rearranges FAMILIES, and 'in' puts P among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something louder or greater is to increase it, as a speaker boosts sound.

clue.text: Insect for example making Darwin's case anew

indicators.note: making here means forming the new outer case round the inner letters

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the outer letters, the case, are stripped so a new case can go round the remaining letters

parts.note: the surname of the naturalist Charles Darwin

explanation.surface: A naturalist's specimen box is rebuilt for a creepy-crawly.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip DARWIN of its case (D and N) to leave ARWI, then rehouse it in a new case, EG.
explanation.definitionFit: This pincered creature is a common garden bug, an example of an insect.

clue.text: Like taking part in merrymaking

indicators.note: a part taken from within the word gives the letters

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys joining in the festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' poses as a verb meaning enjoy but is an adjective meaning similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Related or similar in nature, as in being kindred to something.

clue.text: Order parting gift after Queen makes way for husband

indicators.note: one thing making way for another means it steps aside and is replaced by it

parts.note: a bequest is something left in a will, a gift from someone who has departed

explanation.surface: A legacy is handed over once the monarch gives up her place to her consort.
explanation.walkthrough: In BEQUEST, QU 'makes way for' H, leaving BEHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or instruction, as in acting at someone's bidding.

clue.text: Drug brought about everything in break-up of one band

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word inside the rearranged letters
a break-up scatters the letters into a new order
brought about means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Narcotics caused a group to split up entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' turns ALL into LLA, and 'in' puts it into BEDONNA, the 'break-up of' ONE BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade yields a poison used medicinally, an example of a drug.

clue.text: Worry I'm amused about a scoundrel getting upset

indicators.note: about means around, so the laughter surrounds the rest

parts.note: he he is a sound of laughter

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A cheerful onlooker laughs at a villain falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns CAD into DAC; HE HE goes 'about' A plus DAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causing persistent trouble or anxiety is a nuisance or problem.

clue.text: White Christmas may ultimately embody present time

indicators.note: embody means contain within a body, so the word goes inside
ultimately means at the end, so the final letters are used

parts.note: now is the present time

explanation.surface: Perhaps this year's Christmas will finally bring snow.
explanation.walkthrough: S and Y from the ends of 'Christmas may' go round NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in snow means white, the shade of fresh snowfall.

clue.text: Strands of story resume with characters going up to university

parts.note: a fib is a tall story, a small lie

indicators.text: with characters going up to university
indicators.note: letters are removed from the end back as far as U, the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Threads of a tale continue as the cast heads off to college.
explanation.walkthrough: From RESUME, the characters from the end back to U ('university') go, leaving RES.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibres are thin threads, the same as strands of yarn or hair.

clue.text: Come to terms with colonial rule disappearing

indicators.note: disappearing means vanishing, so the letter leaves the word

parts.note: a colonial is a settler in a colony

explanation.surface: Accepting that empire's rule is ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach an agreement over a dispute is to resolve it by agreeing terms.

clue.text: Neutral international power controlled by military

indicators.note: being controlled by something is being held within its grip, so the letter sits inside the military word

parts.note: martial means relating to war or the armed forces
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A global force run by the army claims to take no side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unbiased and not favouring either side is what neutrality means.

clue.text: Dwelling on losing final pair leads to disappointing exit

indicators.note: the last two letters are dropped from the synonym for on

parts.note: on in the sense of concerning, as in a talk on poetry

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone broods on how dropping the last two points brought about a dismal knockout from a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing final pair' cuts ABOUT to ABO; 'leads to' gives D and E from 'disappointing exit'. 'Dwelling on' looks like one phrase meaning brooding, but 'Dwelling' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a home or residence, a formal synonym for where one lives.

clue.text: Peel complimentary dried fruit

indicators.note: peel means strip off the outer layer, here the first and last letters

parts.note: complimentary remarks are praising ones

explanation.surface: Free candied peel and dried fruit, perhaps on offer at a baking stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complimentary' poses as free of charge but means flattering; peeling PRAISING leaves RAISIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is the classic example of dried fruit.

clue.text: Agent of change given role encompassing country short of capital

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the shortened country goes inside

parts.note: an actor given a role has been cast

indicators.note: capital here is the first letter, which the country's name lacks

parts.note: Italy is a European country

explanation.surface: A spy is assigned a part in a nation that has run out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' poses as money but is the first letter: 'short of capital' drops it from the country, and 'encompassing' wraps the role word round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry and figuratively, a catalyst speeds up or triggers change without being consumed.

clue.text: Inducing 6 perhaps to vandalise heroes' tomb

definitions.note: 6 down is a worry, so this means causing worry, as an adjective

indicators.note: vandalising damages and wrecks, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Desecrating a memorial to the fallen is likely to cause upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 6 down, so read it as 'causing a worry, perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoying or troublesome things cause anxiety, a nuisance to deal with.

clue.text: Hide being almost on the breadline

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money, living on the breadline

explanation.surface: Someone poor tries to stay out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is everyday British slang for broke; 'almost' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide is an animal's pelt or skin, the material leather is made from.

clue.text: Hero (and common criminal) in Fifty Shades of Grey?

indicators.note: criminal used as a word for wrong or bad, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the hero in the erotic novel just an ordinary crook?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HERO and COMMON are mixed up. The book title is a misdirection: fifty shades of grey, literally, is an image in one colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally many tones of grey with no other colour describes a black-and-white image.

clue.text: Talk about soldier returning home for spring

indicators.note: about means around, so the speech word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to orate is to give a speech

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
in means at home

explanation.surface: A speech about a serviceman coming home in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' poses as the season but is a verb meaning arise; GI is the usual crossword soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from a source is to arise or start from it.

clue.text: Put back in control over unfinished match

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so this comes first

parts.note: to rein in is to control

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a vesta is a short wax match

explanation.surface: Someone regains command after an abandoned game.
explanation.walkthrough: A VESTA is a type of match; 'unfinished' leaves VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest money again is to place funds back into something.

clue.text: Imploring b___ fools to retreat and contain attack

parts.note: the blanked word stands for a swear word beginning with b, giving just its first letter

indicators.note: contain means hold inside, so the attack goes into the reversed fools
retreating means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a goose is a silly person, so geese are fools
to chin someone is to punch them on the chin

explanation.surface: An exasperated commander begs his blankety-blank idiots to fall back and hold off the assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' reverses the fools, giving ESEEG, and 'contain' puts the attack inside it before its final letter. To chin someone is to punch them.
explanation.definitionFit: Begging someone earnestly is pleading with them, the same as entreating.

clue.text: Using some kohlrabi's questionable in this

indicators.note: Using some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether using a dubious vegetable in this soup is wise.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue doubles as the definition: some kohlrabi might well go into this creamy soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich creamy soup is the kind of dish that vegetables like kohlrabi might be put in.

clue.text: Farmer perhaps spending the two pounds he has in bank

indicators.note: spending means paying out, so the pounds leave the word

parts.note: a tiller is one who tills the soil, a farmer for example
L is the abbreviation for pound, and the tiller contains two

explanation.surface: A farmer withdraws his last couple of quid from his account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' poses as a place for money but means a row, as in banks of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of seats or oars is a row or level, the same as a rising tier.

clue.text: Republican following one providing support for The House

definitions.text: one providing support for The House

parts.note: after means following

explanation.surface: A Republican backing a Congress member in the House of Representatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The House' looks like the American chamber, but means a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof beam holds up a building's roof, so it supports a house.

clue.text: Old copper that's still used by cooks

definitions.meaning: early British police officers were named after Sir Robert Peel, who founded the force
a kitchen tool for removing vegetable skins

explanation.surface: A retired policeman is still helpful in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: PEELER was an early nickname for a London policeman, after founder Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a nineteenth-century constable and a kitchen gadget for skinning potatoes share this name.

clue.text: Is my religious education an outcome of this place?

indicators.note: the letters come out as a new arrangement of the words given

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A student asks whether their religious training resulted from attending a particular college.
explanation.walkthrough: IS MY, RE and AN are rearranged ('outcome of'); the clue also hints at a college for priests.
explanation.definitionFit: A college training priests is the place where religious education is the outcome.

clue.text: Male friend scratching head is confused

indicators.note: scratching here means removing, and head is the first letter

parts.note: a buddy is a friend

explanation.surface: A man's pal scratches his head in puzzlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' looks like the gesture of puzzlement but removes the B of BUDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled or unclear thinking is muddy, like murky water.

clue.text: Complaint about fake news possibly reduced trust

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened complaint goes round the untruth
reduced means made shorter, so one letter goes

parts.note: a beef is slang for a grievance
fake news is an example of a lie

explanation.surface: Grumbling about misinformation has weakened public confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: BEEF is 'reduced' to BEF, which goes 'about' LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust and faith overlap: to have faith in something is to be convinced of it.

clue.text: Members of pack close to tears after point of no return?

indicators.note: after puts the tennis point before the last letter

parts.note: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return, winning a point

indicators.note: close means end, so the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Pack animals near weeping after a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point of no return' poses as the moment of no turning back.
explanation.definitionFit: The top cards in each suit are members of a deck of cards.

clue.text: A French affaire d'honneur failing to reach conclusion is not comme il faut

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: an affair of honour is a duel

explanation.surface: A French duel abandoned before the end is a breach of etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: Comme il faut is French for proper or as it should be, so its negation means excessive or improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improper or excessive is unwarranted, beyond what is fitting.

clue.text: Let social maverick swing both ways

indicators.note: a maverick is unorthodox and wayward, so the letters go astray

explanation.surface: An invitation to an unconventional person to be openly bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving to and fro like a pendulum is to sway back and forth in both directions.

clue.text: Evergreen tree harbouring strain from the east

indicators.note: read from the east is right to left, so the letters run backwards
harbouring means holding within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the elm is a tree
to strain is to try hard

explanation.surface: A tree that keeps its leaves carries a variety from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' makes ELTRYM, and 'from the east' reads it backwards. 'Evergreen tree' looks like one definition, but 'tree' is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This shrub keeps its glossy leaves all year, so it is an example of an evergreen plant.

clue.text: Vet witnessed inspiring commander's limits

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the letters are drawn inside

parts.note: something witnessed has been seen

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A veterinarian observed the edges of an officer's influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' poses as an animal doctor but means check, as in vetting candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet candidates is to check them carefully, as in screening applicants.
